To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the overlap Dirac operator has a family index which can be used to define a topological charge for the gauge fields, which in turn is used to show that the topological sectors of the space of gauge fields are nontrivial, and that these nontrivial topological features can be used to explain the existence of obstructions to the gauge fixing problem.
the space of lattice SU(2) gauge fields on the four-dimensional torus is a noncontractible two-sphere, and that the space of SU(3) lattice gauge fields is a nontrivial four-dimensional sphere.
the topological features of SU(N) gauge theories on the 4-dimensional lattice, N⩾2, can be understood in terms of the families index theory for overlap lattice Dirac operators.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a number of issues related to gauge fixing, families index theorem, and the topology of the space of gauge fields on a lattice, with the ultimate goal to understand better the nature of the Gribov ambiguity in lattice field theory.
the topological features of lattice gauge fields and with the relation of these features to gauge fixing and to the Gribov ambiguity in the continuum.
a topological characterization of the space of all lattice gauge fields, and with the topological properties of its subspaces corresponding to different values of the topological charge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the space of SU(3) lattice gauge fields contains a contractible 4-sphere, and that there is a canonical connection with singularities on this 4-sphere.
the space of SU(3) lattice gauge fields is not a smooth manifold but rather a stratified space, with the topological sectors as the strata, and the Gribov horizon as the boundary of the strata.
the topological features of gauge fields are not lost in the lattice approximation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new way to understand and characterize the Gribov ambiguity, which has been a longstanding issue in lattice gauge theory.
the space of lattice configurations is a non-trivial topological space.
the topological structure of the space of gauge fields is closely related to the existence or not of gauge fixings free of the Gribov ambiguity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
topological features of gauge fields are intimately connected to the existence of certain gauge fixings, and the latter are intimately connected to families index theory for Dirac-type operators.
the overlap lattice Dirichlet fermionic determinant, which is a topological invariant of the space of gauge fields, can be used as a tool to understand topological aspects of lattice gauge theory.
the space of lattice fields is a nontrivial space with topological features.
